assessment.atom: The [atom id] leaf carries the established ID format from R2699, has a separate new Summary and Subject requiring fresh ID, and imposes 0..1 values only when selected; it is suitable for an actual Draft subject to canonical Draft metadata and parent/group integration.
assessment.scope_unit: The leaf copies [scope unit] from R2700 but does not itself say the value is a Scope Unit ID. The copied format name alone does not establish the latest IDs-only exclusion of paths and name suffixes in the source read. Add Claim Prose: “The value is the stable ID of the containing Scope Unit.” Also verify the [scope unit] Format admits exactly those IDs; otherwise reconcile its existing authority in the source batch.
assessment.cardinality: Each leaf has 0..1 values because the parent selects exactly one of two alternatives; neither leaf makes both alternatives mandatory. Their children are prohibited. The parent mapping, root encoding and bootstrap remain held and must be coordinated before adoption.
assessment.identity: Both changed Summaries and Subjects require new IDs, rather than reusing R2699/R2700. Existing source declarations remain pinned in the packet; no Current or native Draft may be overwritten by these previews.
assessment.notation: Both use prospective :: notation, so actual Draft creation is possible as proposal material but requires governing notation integration before admission.

limits: Review is bounded to leaf readiness and does not resolve root encoding or assert Current adoption.

repair.change: Use existing [string] Format and add the stable-ID-only Prose Claim. Prior hold remains historical evidence; parent group/root encoding and coordinated adoption remain open.
